dossiers.title: Devil May Cry 4 Special Edition
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players emphasize precise, expressive third-person melee combat built around chaining attacks, switching weapons and styles, and improving execution, rather than casual button-mashing.

The Special Edition's Vergil, Trish and Lady meaningfully change fighting tactics: teleporting and sword combinations, crowd-control lightning attacks, and a strongly gun-focused character, alongside higher-density challenge modes.
Players repeatedly advise using a gamepad on PC: keyboard-only play is cumbersome, mouse support was lacking in the reviewed release, and some older controllers had recognition issues.
Unlocking moves and bonus costumes and refining character-specific combos provides goals beyond clearing the story; some items are also offered as optional paid time-savers.

The extra playable characters mostly reuse the established campaign environments and offer only brief introductory or closing cinematics rather than fully bespoke story sequences, making combat replay the principal additional content.
Mastering timing, weapon selection and character techniques gives the combat substantial depth, while some players object to the demanding high-difficulty combat and camera behavior.

A detailed early PC player report notes motion blur and variable optimization; another 2025 review still describes startup problems requiring unofficial workarounds. These dated reports do not establish that every contemporary setup is affected.

Russian-language players discussing this exact 2015 Special Edition objected to missing official Russian subtitles and voice support, contrasting it with the localized original release; their opinions of the original translation and voice work diverged.

Community feedback is mixed on the port: one player reports loading-screen crashes, another reports an update-related launch failure, while a separate player says the game runs acceptably after an update. These are individual, incompletely dated reports rather than a verified universal defect.

dossiers.title: As Long As You're Here
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The experience is a first-person, low-action narrative walk through domestic routines such as tending plants or knitting; familiar activities grow disorienting as the protagonist's memory and surroundings shift.

Most players describe a deliberately short, roughly one-to-two-hour story intended for a single sitting; some welcome its density and lack of filler, while others wish there were more time with the characters.
Players with personal or caregiving experience of dementia report that the shifting perception, loss of agency and family themes feel unusually empathetic and emotionally credible.
The narrative puts the older protagonist's changing recollections, relationships and domestic setting ahead of conventional combat, extensive puzzles or complex character upgrades.
Players particularly praise the restrained visual style, soundtrack and quietly distressing atmosphere as support for the intimate family story rather than a spectacle-driven presentation.

One detailed player account identifies limited scene replay options, sometimes slow text reveal and briefly uncomfortable shifting animations as small but noticeable interface and presentation trade-offs.

An exact-product Russian-language Steam reviewer in November 2025 noted the absence of Russian language support, while still finding the short story understandable; the Steam product listing also omits Russian among supported languages.

An early community participant found the short runtime disappointing despite praising the gentle depiction of illness and family loss; other players considered the short length appropriate to the emotional weight.

conflicts.statement: Opinions diverge on whether the approximately one-hour format is an asset of the focused emotional narrative or leaves its characters and scenes underdeveloped.

dossiers.title: Alpha Protocol™
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The espionage RPG mixes stealth, third-person shooting, close-range encounters, hacking and information gathering; players find the premise distinctive but the physical action noticeably dated and uneven.
Decisions made during dialogue and missions influence allies, future scenes and possible outcomes; mission order and which contacts to pursue can change later interactions.
Reports of inconsistent enemy awareness, awkward controls, collision quirks, rough animations and intrusive enemy spawning are persistent caveats to the otherwise unusual role-playing design.
Skill development, firearms and other equipment permit different agent approaches, yet some players find the gear economy poorly differentiated relative to the narrative choices.
Hub-like international missions and their varying locales support flexible mission order, while some return players perceive abrupt enemy placement and an uneven, loosely joined ending.
Agent contacts, timed conversational decisions and branching loyalties are frequent strengths of the spy-thriller experience; opinions of the overarching story's coherence are more divided.
Some players find the hacking minigame and unpredictable stealth detection more frustrating than strategically challenging, occasionally hindering otherwise viable mission approaches.

A 2023 Russian-language player account describes rapidly changing subtitles and unclear translated dialogue-choice labels, which can obscure decisions; this is dated historical feedback, not a verified present build-wide issue.

In 2025 an exact-app community discussion noted that Steam and GOG releases differ in certain compatibility and controller enhancements; at least one player said the Steam build recognized XInput controllers. These comments are release-specific and do not prove universal present-day compatibility.

Players value replaying to witness different alliances and later narrative consequences, but such variability coexists with a relatively fixed protagonist identity and limited cosmetic personalization.
